explanation: The base case only fires when `n === 1`. For `n === 0` (or any negative starting value), the sequence of calls goes `0, -1, -2, -3, ...` and never equals `1`, so the recursion never hits its base case and blows the call stack. The base case should be `n <= 1` (or explicitly handle `n === 0`).
prompt: This factorial function crashes for one specific input. What's the bug?
choices: The base case only checks `n === 1`, so calling `factorial(0)` decrements past 1 into negative numbers forever and never terminates
It will incorrectly return `NaN` for any negative input because of implicit type coercion
The recursive call passes `n - 1` instead of `n + 1`, causing infinite recursion
Multiplying `n * factorial(n - 1)` will overflow for large positive integers, producing incorrect results
